records.text: Owens said Thomas H. Patrick was Merrill Lynch's executive vice chairman and CEO and worked there for 25 years in Chicago.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: And I'm going to tell you more. Thomas Patrick was the executive vice chairman and CEO of Merrill Lynch. ... That's wealth management investment firm. He worked there for 25 years in Chicago. Big guy, boss, very connected, very political.

verification.notes: Merrill Lynch’s SEC filing and Patrick’s obituary confirm he became executive vice chairman and earlier worked in the Chicago office. They do not identify him as CEO; he returned to Merrill in 1982 and retired in 2003, about 21 years, and moved to New York in 1989. The title, tenure, and Chicago characterization are therefore partly wrong.

sources.title: Merrill Lynch & Co. 2003 SEC filing
sources.relevance: Lists Patrick as executive vice chairman and his earlier roles, not CEO.

sources.title: Thomas H. Patrick obituary
sources.relevance: Provides his Chicago-to-New York career chronology and 1982-2003 Merrill tenure.

records.text: Owens said Thomas H. Patrick was escorted from his office in 2003 amid accusations that he orchestrated a political smear campaign against Eliot Spitzer.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Until 2003, he was unceremoniously escorted out of his office for a scandal in which he was accused of, of all things, orchestrating a political smear campaign against Elliot Spitzer, who he didn't like.

verification.notes: Contemporaneous reporting confirms an internal investigation into whether Patrick sought to fund media content disparaging Eliot Spitzer and that he abruptly left in 2003. It also reports Merrill concluded the matter was false. The specific claim that he was escorted from his office is not supported by the reviewed record.

sources.title: Plan to Discredit Spitzer Alleged
sources.relevance: Contemporaneous report describes the investigation, Patrick’s departure, and Merrill’s conclusion that the matter was false.

records.text: Owens said Merrill Lynch was acquired by Bank of America in 2008 following the financial crisis.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: You will note and remember perhaps in 2008 following the financial crisis, Merrill Lynch was acquired by Bank of America. So it became Bank of America Merrill Lynch.

verification.notes: Bank of America’s September 15, 2008 SEC filing and press release document its agreement to acquire Merrill Lynch during the financial crisis.

sources.title: Bank of America September 15, 2008 Form 8-K
sources.relevance: Official filing documents the Merrill Lynch acquisition agreement.

records.text: Owens said Stephen Philip and Tyler Bowyer's father worked at Bank of America Merrill Lynch in Chicago at the same time.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: That's going to become relevant because Danny Phillips' father, Stephen Phillips, worked for Bank of America Merrill Lynch in Chicago, Chicago, Chicago, Chicago everywhere. ... At the same time that he worked at Bank of America Merrill Lynch in Chicago, so did Tyler Bowyer's father, major executive at Bank of America Merrill Lynch.

verification.notes: Searches found no reliable employment records establishing both men’s identities, roles, locations, and overlapping dates. The claim appears derived from private or removed profile material and cannot be independently confirmed.

records.text: Owens said Dennis Frantzve was involved in the military and then worked for Bank of America Merrill Lynch.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: He was also involved in the military before that, as you guys know. After he left the military, he went to work for Bank of America Merrill Lynch and then stopped quickly to show Erika around the Black Sea rotational force.

verification.notes: Live searches did not locate a reliable public employment or service record tying a Dennis Frantzve to both the military and Bank of America Merrill Lynch. The identity and claimed sequence remain unresolved.

records.text: Owens said Donald Trump appointed John C. Phelan as secretary of the Navy despite Phelan having no military experience and a career background in banking.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Trump appointed a guy with literally zero military experience into that position, crucial position. ... So he appoints this guy John C. Phelan and his whole background is in banking.

verification.notes: The Senate record confirms John C. Phelan's 2025 confirmation as secretary of the Navy. Official Navy biography and military reporting describe his investment-management career and lack of prior military service. These sources support the appointment, no-military-experience, and finance-background components.
